evidence.positive: Staged fresh demo-demo adult patients (DOB 1980, 80 kg, 4,000 mg ceiling) via the admin API, added a prior m-acetaminophen-iv bolus with POST /api/admin/bolus at a chosen offset, evicted the Valkey patients/demo-demo/<pmrn> cache entry, then as loopuser called POST /api/cds/medication-selection and POST /api/cds/medication-dose (1,000 mg). P1: 4,000 mg given 1,425 min (23h45m) earlier -> selection returned no acetaminophen max-dose results; app log: 'Rule evaluated: a-acetaminophen-max-dose-scan -> false cumulative ACETAMINOPHEN dose (0 mg) below max threshold (4,000 mg)', 'w-acetaminophen-max-dose -> false cumulative ACETAMINOPHEN dose (0 mg) below warning threshold (3,000 mg)', 'a-acetaminophen-max-dose-save -> false cumulative dose (0.0 mg) not above max dose (4,000 mg)'. P2: 3,500 mg at 23h45m + 1,000 mg dose check -> no warning and no save alert. B1: 4,000 mg at 1,411 min (23h31m) -> nothing fired, so the buffer boundary holds on the excluded side.
evidence.negative: Same staging with the prior dose inside the 23h30m window. N1: 4,000 mg at 1,395 min (23h15m) -> a-acetaminophen-max-dose-scan fired (needsAction true, prompt 'Patient has received 4,000 mg of acetaminophen in the past 24 hours. Max dose of acetaminophen is 4,000 mg in 24 hours. Recommend alternative medication.') and w-acetaminophen-max-dose fired with CUMULATIVE_24_HOUR_DOSE_MG 4,000; the save rule abstained 'max dose already reached prior to this dose attempt'. N2: 3,500 mg at 23h15m -> warning fired (cumulative 3,500 of 4,000 mg) and the 1,000 mg dose check returned the a-acetaminophen-max-dose-save alert 'Patient has received 3,500 mg of acetaminophen in the past 24 hours'. B2: 4,000 mg at 1,409 min (23h29m) -> scan and warning fired, so the boundary holds on the counted side. Early-redose row of the ticket (15 min buffer, pre-existing code): 1,000 mg at 350 min -> no a-acetaminophen-early-redose; at 340 min -> fired 'Acetaminophen Dosing is Q6H'.
evidence.red_check: Compiled the parent commit's AcetaminophenCalculator (plain Duration.ofHours(24), confirmed via javap that CUMULATIVE_WINDOW/plusMinutes are absent) with the container's javac, backed up the shipped class (md5 08f46c2400bc892799d1b9e772a80793, copy saved to scratch), copied the pre-fix class over /app/classes/com/guided/orci/engine/rule/medication/utils/AcetaminophenCalculator.class and restarted the container. R1: the identical 4,000 mg at 23h45m scenario then went red: selection returned a-acetaminophen-max-dose-scan and w-acetaminophen-max-dose with cumulative 4,000 mg, and the log carries 'Rule evaluated: a-acetaminophen-max-dose-scan -> true' for patient 01a178d5-b166-7daf-a30e-2685ecd76ae5. Restored the backup (md5 matches the shipped checksum), restarted again (3 'Started OrciApplication' boots in the log), and R2 re-ran 4,000 mg at 23h45m: no results, log back to 'cumulative ACETAMINOPHEN dose (0 mg) below max threshold'. The data flip (23h15m vs 23h45m, N1/N2 vs P1/P2) was also performed against the shipped class.

caveats: Only the adult >= 50 kg tier (4,000 mg ceiling, 3,000 mg warning threshold) was exercised at runtime; the 75 mg/kg, pediatric 3,750 mg and infant 60 mg/kg tiers share the same CUMULATIVE_WINDOW constant but were not run.
Exercised through the same /api/cds/medication-selection and /api/cds/medication-dose endpoints the UI calls, not through the browser; the alert and banner rendering was not viewed.
The early-redose 15-minute buffer in the ticket table was already in code before this PR (3h45m/5h45m thresholds); it was confirmed at runtime but no change to it shipped under OR-3009.
KetorolacMaxDoseRule also runs through the changed AbstractMaxDoseRule (its window now comes from the max dose record); only its unit test was added, it was not exercised at runtime.
The compliance side (companion commit marking buffered Mayo firings compliant under OR-3025) was not exercised.
Prior doses were single IV mg boluses; combination tablets counted by acetaminophen content were not exercised.

automation.assessment: The PR added unit tests for the 23h30m boundary on the scan, warning, save and ketorolac rules plus the calculator window, so the boundary itself is locked in. qa-suite has no acetaminophen max-dose coverage at all (the only acetaminophen reference is a Mayo HL7 attribution spec). A browser-free API pair in clinical-rules would lock in the end-to-end path (admin bolus -> cache -> selection/dose endpoints) that unit tests cannot see.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A 4,000 mg acetaminophen dose given 23h45m earlier was not counted, so the scan alert, warning and save alert all stayed silent on the next selection and 1,000 mg dose check.
Negative: The same dose given 23h15m earlier was counted, firing the scan alert and warning, and a 3,500 mg prior dose plus 1,000 mg fired the save alert.
Red check: Running the pre-fix calculator class with the plain 24-hour window made the 23h45m case fire the scan alert, and restoring the shipped class silenced it again.

Automation: Unit tests from the PR cover the boundary; a browser-free qa-suite pair through the selection and dose endpoints is proposed.
